questions.question: Which deity is associated with the mythology behind Mohiniyattam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Vishnu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mohiniyattam** is a classical dance form from the state of **Kerala**, known for its graceful, swaying movements that mimic the palm trees and rivers of the region.
 
• The name is derived from the words **Mohini**, meaning an enchantress or a woman who attracts, and **Attam**, meaning dance.
 
• According to Hindu mythology, **Lord Vishnu** took the form of **Mohini** to assist the **Devas** (gods) in their battle against the **Asuras** (demons).</li&g

questions.question: The Sundarbans are famous for which type of natural vegetation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mangrove forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sundarbans** constitute the largest contiguous **mangrove forest** ecosystem in the world, covering approximately 10,000 square kilometers across **India** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• Located at the mouth of the **Ganges**, **Brahmaputra**, and **Meghna** rivers on the **Bay of Bengal**, this region is a complex network of tidal waterways, mudflats, and small islands.
 
• The vegetation is dominated by **halophytes**, which are salt-tolerant plant species adapted to survive in harsh **intertidal zones** and saline soil conditions.
 
• The forest is named after the **Sundari tree** (**Heritiera fomes**), which provides high-quality timber and is the most abundant tree species in the area.
 
• Plants in this ecosystem feature specialized adaptations such as **pneumatophores** (breathing roots) that grow vertically upwards to facilitate gas exchange in **anaerobic** waterlogged soil.
 
• The **Sundarbans** is designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and a **Ramsar Site**, serving as a critical habitat for the endangered **Royal Bengal Tiger**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropical Evergreen Forests**:

 
 
• These occur in regions with more than **200 cm** of annual rainfall and temperatures between **25°C to 27°C**.
 
• Commonly found in the **Western Ghats**, **Northeast India**, and the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**.
 
 
 
• **Desert Vegetation**:
 
 
• Consists of **xerophytic** plants like cacti and thorny bushes found in **arid** regions with less than **50 cm** of rainfall, primarily in **Rajasthan** and **Gujarat**.
 
 
 
• **Alpine Meadows**:
 
 
• These are found in the high-altitude regions of the **Himalayas**, generally above **3,000 meters**, characterized by short grasses and **mosses**.

questions.question: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) requires completion of investigation in sexual offenses within:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 months**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023**, which replaced the **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)**, mandates a strict timeline for the completion of investigations in cases of **sexual offenses**.
 
• Under **Section 193(1)** of the **BNSS**, the investigation into offenses relating to **rape** and **sexual assault** must be completed within a period of **two months**.
 
• This specific timeframe applies to offenses defined under **Sections 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70, 71, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, and 79** of the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**.
 
• The **two-month period** is calculated from the date on which the **information** (FIR) was first recorded by the **officer-in-charge** of the police station.
 
• This provision ensures **expeditious justice** for survivors of sexual violence by preventing procedural delays at the **investigative stage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medical Examination:**

 
 
• According to **Section 184** of the **BNSS**, the **medical examination** of a victim of a sexual offense must be performed by a **Registered Medical Practitioner** within **24 hours** of the police receiving information about the crime.
 
 
 
• **Victim Rights and Updates:**
 
 
• The **BNSS** emphasizes **victim-centric justice**, requiring police to provide updates on the **progress of the investigation** to the victim or informant within **90 days**.
 
 
 
• **Effective Date:**
 
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita**, along with the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita** and the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam**, came into official force across India on **July 1, 2024**.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Supervision:**
 
 
• The **Magistrate** is empowered to monitor the investigation to ensure compliance with these **statutory timelines**, fostering greater **accountability** within the law enforcement agencies.

questions.question: Which of the following tax was levied on cultivation under the administration of Alauddin Khalji?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kharaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khalji** (1296−1316) introduced comprehensive agrarian reforms to maximize state revenue and maintain a powerful **standing army**.
 
• **Kharaj** was the specific agricultural land tax levied on the produce of the soil, which formed the backbone of the Sultanate's economy.
 
• Under his reign, the **Kharaj** was increased to **50 percent** of the total produce, representing the highest tax rate imposed by any Delhi Sultan.
 
• He implemented a system of **land measurement** known as **Masahat**, ensuring that tax was calculated based on the actual area under cultivation using the **Biswa** as a standard unit.
 
• To prevent local intermediaries like **Khuts** and **Muqaddams** from exploiting peasants or evading taxes, he abolished their traditional privileges and brought them under the same tax regime as ordinary cultivators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahzar**:

 
 
• It refers to a **formal petition** or a public attestation; most famously, the **Infallibility Decree** of **1579**.
 
• This decree was issued by the Mughal Emperor **Akbar** to establish his supremacy over the **Ulema** in matters of religious interpretation.
 
 
 
• **Amil**:
 
 
• A high-ranking **revenue official** responsible for the assessment and collection of taxes at the **Pargana** level.
 
• They were instrumental in documenting **cultivation patterns** and ensuring that the revenue reached the central treasury.
 
 
 
• **Other Taxes under Alauddin Khalji**:
 
 
• **Ghari**: A specialized tax imposed on the **residential houses** of the subjects.
 
• **Chari**: A **grazing tax** levied on the pasturage of milch animals and cattle.
 
• **Zakat**: A **religious tax** paid by Muslims, typically 2.5 percent of their total wealth, used for charitable purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from United States of America?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Preamble of the constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Preamble** of the Indian Constitution is a borrowed feature from the **United States of America**, which was the first nation in the world to begin its constitution with a preamble.
 
• The phrase **'We, the People of India'** is directly inspired by the opening words of the **US Constitution**, which reads **'We, the People of the United States'**, signifying that power resides in the citizens.
 
• The Preamble serves as an introduction to the **Constitution of India**, outlining the fundamental values, philosophy, and objectives such as **Sovereignty, Socialism, Secularism, Democracy,** and **Republic**.
 
• Other significant features adopted from the **USA** include **Fundamental Rights**, the **Independence of the Judiciary**, **Judicial Review**, the **Impeachment of the President**, and the **Removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**:

 
 
• These were not part of the original constitution but were added via the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** based on the **Swaran Singh Committee** recommendations.
 
• The concept was borrowed from the constitution of the **USSR** (present-day Russia).
 
 
 
• **Concept of Republic**:
 
 
• The ideals of **Republic** and the principles of **Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity** in the Preamble were borrowed from the **French Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Freedom of Trade and Commerce**:
 
 
• Provisions relating to the **Freedom of trade, commerce, and intercourse** (Article 301 to 307) and the concept of a **Joint Sitting of the two Houses of Parliament** were inspired by the **Australian Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**:
 
 
• The **DPSP** (Articles 36-51), which guide the state in making laws for social and economic justice, were borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**.

questions.question: Which state government established Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar Abhyaran as a new wildlife sanctuary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Madhya Pradesh** state government officially notified the establishment of the **Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar Abhyaran** (Wildlife Sanctuary) in the **Sagar district**.
 
• This sanctuary spans an area of approximately **258.64 square kilometers**, primarily utilizing forest land from the **North Sagar Forest Division**.
 
• The sanctuary is designed to facilitate a protected corridor for wildlife movement between the **Nauradehi Wildlife Sanctuary** and the **Veerangana Durgavati Wildlife Sanctuary**.
 
• Naming the sanctuary after **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, the principal architect of the **Indian Constitution**, serves as a tribute to his legacy in his home state of birth (Mhow, MP).
 
• The notification was issued under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**, aiming to conserve the biodiversity of the **Vindhyan landscape** and protect species like **Tigers**, **Leopards**, and **Sloth Bears**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madhya Pradesh Forest Statistics:**

 
 
• Commonly known as the **Tiger State of India**, Madhya Pradesh recorded the highest tiger population of **785** in the **2022 Tiger Census**.
 
• The state possesses the largest **forest cover** in India by area, as per the **India State of Forest Report (ISFR)**.
 
• It houses several world-renowned **National Parks**, including **Kanha**, **Bandhavgarh**, **Pench**, and **Panna**.
 
• The **Nauradehi Wildlife Sanctuary** is the largest sanctuary in the state, covering parts of Sagar, Damoh, and Narsinghpur districts.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• The establishment of this sanctuary is part of a broader strategy to manage the **Ken-Betwa River Interlinking Project** impact by creating alternative habitats for displaced wildlife.
 
• **Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve** was recently notified as the **7th Tiger Reserve** in Madhya Pradesh, integrating areas of Nauradehi and Durgavati sanctuaries.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first Indian mission dedicated to observing the Sun?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aditya L-1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aditya L-1** is the first dedicated **Indian space mission** designed specifically to observe and study the **Sun** from space.
 
• The mission was successfully launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** on **September 2, 2023**, utilizing the **PSLV-C57** launch vehicle from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota.
 
• The spacecraft is placed in a **halo orbit** around the **Lagrange Point 1 (L1)** of the Sun-Earth system, which is approximately **1.5 million kilometers** away from Earth, allowing it to view the Sun continuously without occultation or eclipses.
 
• The mission carries **seven payloads** to observe the **photosphere**, **chromosphere**, and the outermost layers of the Sun, known as the **corona**, using electromagnetic and particle detectors.
 
• Its primary scientific objectives include studying the dynamics of the **solar upper atmosphere**, **Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs)**, **solar flares**, and the physics of the **solar corona** and its heating mechanism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hinode (Solar-B)**

 
 
• It is an international mission led by the **Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA)**, in collaboration with **NASA** and the **UK Space Agency**, launched in **2006** to study the Sun's magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Parker Solar Probe**
 
 
• A **NASA** spacecraft launched in **2018** with the mission to 'touch' the Sun by traveling through the **solar corona**, closer than any previous spacecraft.
 
 
 
• **SOHO (Solar and Heliospheric Observatory)**
 
 
• A joint project between the **European Space Agency (ESA)** and **NASA**, launched in **December 1995** to study the Sun from its deep core to the outer corona and the solar wind.

questions.question: Hutti Gold Mines is located in which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hutti Gold Mines** are situated in the **Raichur district** of the state of **Karnataka**.
 
• It is currently the only operational unit in **India** that produces gold by mining and processing gold ore from its primary source.
 
• The mines are managed by **Hutti Gold Mines Limited (HGML)**, which is a **Government of Karnataka** undertaking.
 
• Historically, these mines are among the oldest in the world, with archaeological data suggesting mining activity dates back to the **Pre-Ashokan period**, more than **2,000 years** ago.
 
• Geologically, the gold deposits are found within the **Hutti-Maski Schist Belt**, an **Archean** greenstone belt characterized by auriferous quartz veins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karnataka**:

 
 
• The state contributes nearly **99%** of **India** total gold production.
 
• It was home to the **Kolar Gold Fields (KGF)** in the **Kolar district**, which were among the deepest mines in the world before closing in **2001**.
 
 
 
• **Jharkhand**:
 
 
• Renowned for its vast coal reserves in the **Damodar Valley** and iron ore in the **Singhbhum** region.
 
• The **Subarnarekha River** is traditionally known for the presence of gold particles in its alluvial sands.
 
 
 
• **Odisha**:
 
 
• The state is the leading producer of **Iron Ore**, **Chromite**, **Bauxite**, and **Manganese** in **India**.
 
• Key mining hubs include the **Keonjhar**, **Mayurbhanj**, and **Sundargarh** districts.
 
 
 
• **Bihar**:
 
 
• Post-bifurcation, Bihar retains significant deposits of **Limestone**, **Mica**, and **Pyrite**.
 
• The **Amjhore** area in **Rohtas** is particularly noted for its **Pyrite** (iron sulfide) deposits.

questions.question: When did Mumbai Indians Women win their first WPL (Women's Premier League) title?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2023**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mumbai Indians Women** (MI-W) secured their first **Women's Premier League (WPL)** title in the inaugural season held in **2023**.
 
• The final match took place on **March 26, 2023**, at the **Brabourne Stadium** in **Mumbai**, where they faced the **Delhi Capitals**.
 
• Led by captain **Harmanpreet Kaur**, the Mumbai Indians successfully chased a target of **132 runs**, winning the match by **7 wickets** with three balls to spare.
 
• The **Delhi Capitals**, batting first, were restricted to **131/9** in their 20 overs, while Mumbai Indians reached **134/3** in **19.3 overs** to claim the historic trophy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Awards and Achievements in WPL 2023**:

 
 
• **Hayley Matthews** of Mumbai Indians was named the **Player of the Tournament** for her exceptional all-round performance, scoring 271 runs and taking 16 wickets.
 
• The **Purple Cap** for the highest wicket-taker was also awarded to **Hayley Matthews**.
 
• The **Orange Cap** for the highest run-scorer was won by **Meg Lanning**, the captain of Delhi Capitals, who scored 345 runs.
 
• **Nat Sciver-Brunt** was awarded the **Player of the Match** in the final for her unbeaten 60 runs.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent Seasons**:
 
 
• The second edition of the WPL was held in **2024**, which was won by **Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB)** after they defeated Delhi Capitals in the final.
 
• The tournament is organized by the **Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI)** to promote women's cricket at the professional level.

questions.question: Who built the city of 'Lal Kot' in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anang Pal Tomar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anang Pal Tomar**, also known as **Anangpal II**, was a ruler from the **Tomar Dynasty** who is historically credited with the establishment of **Delhi** (then known as **Dhillika**).
 
• He built the citadel of **Lal Kot** in the middle of the **11th century**, specifically around **1052 AD**, making it the first fortified city of Delhi.
 
• The **Lal Kot** fortification served as the capital for the **Tomar kings**, located in the present-day **Mehrauli** region of South Delhi.
 
• The **Iron Pillar of Delhi**, which stands in the **Qutub Minar** complex, is believed to have been brought to this location by **Anangpal Tomar** from **Vishnupadagiri** (likely Udayagiri).
 
• Evidence of his reign is found in inscriptions and literary works like the **Prithviraj Raso**, which highlight the **Tomar** lineage's foundational role in Delhi's urban history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prithvi Raj Chauhan**:

 
 
• A legendary ruler of the **Chahamana (Chauhan) Dynasty** who captured Delhi from the Tomars in the **12th century**.
 
• He extended the walls of **Lal Kot** and renamed the expanded city as **Qila Rai Pithora**.
 
 
 
• **Alauddin Khilji**:
 
 
• A prominent ruler of the **Khilji Dynasty** who established the city of **Siri** in **1303 AD**.
 
• This was the second of the seven historical cities of Delhi, built primarily as a military camp to defend against **Mongol invasions**.
 
 
 
• **Humayun**:
 
 
• The second **Mughal Emperor** who laid the foundation of the city of **Dinpanah** in **1533 AD**.
 
• The site later became the location for the **Purana Qila** (Old Fort) after it was reconstructed by **Sher Shah Suri**.

questions.question: In 1875, Dwarkanath Ghose designed his version of the Indian hand-pumped _____ in Calcutta.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harmonium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1875**, **Dwarkanath Ghose** revolutionized the musical instrument industry in India by designing a modified version of the **Harmonium** in **Calcutta** (modern-day **Kolkata**).
 
• Ghose was the founder of the renowned firm **Dwarkin & Son**, a name derived as a portmanteau of **Dwarkanath** and his son.
 
• The original **European harmonium** or **reed organ** was designed to be played with **foot-pedals** to pump air, which was physically incompatible with the traditional **Indian seating posture** where musicians sit on the floor (**Asana**).
 
• Dwarkanath Ghose adapted the instrument by replacing the foot-pedals with **hand-operated bellows** located at the back or front of the instrument, allowing the player to pump air with one hand while playing the **keyboard** with the other.
 
• This innovation made the instrument highly **portable**, easy to handle, and robust enough to withstand the **tropical climate** of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The **hand-pumped harmonium** quickly became an essential accompaniment for **vocal music**, providing a steady **drone** and melodic support across various genres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harmonium**:

 
 
• It is a **free-reed instrument** that generates sound as air flows past vibrating pieces of thin metal in a frame.
 
• Despite its **Western origins**, it is now deeply embedded in **Hindustani classical**, **Sufi** (such as **Qawwali**), and **devotional music** like **Bhajans** and **Kirtans**.
 
• The instrument was once banned from **All India Radio** (from 1940 to 1971) because purists argued it could not produce **Meend** (glissando) or the **Shrutis** (microtones) essential to **Indian Ragas**.
 
• Key components include the **bellows**, **air chamber**, **reeds** (often made of **brass** or **copper**), and the **keyboard** consisting of keys representing a **tempered scale**.

questions.question: Who is known as the 'God of Ghatam' for popularising the earthen pot instrument, 'Ghatam'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**T. H. Vinayakram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram**, popularly known as **Vikku Vinayakram**, is a world-renowned percussionist and a maestro of the **Ghatam**, an earthenware pot used in **Carnatic music**.
 
• He is widely celebrated as the **God of Ghatam** for his unparalleled speed, rhythmic precision, and for elevating the instrument from a rhythmic accompaniment to a global solo entity.
 
• Vinayakram was a key member of the original line-up of the fusion band **Shakti**, collaborating with legendary artists like **John McLaughlin** and **Ustad Zakir Hussain** to blend Indian classical music with Western jazz.
 
• In **1991**, he created history by becoming the first **South Indian musician** to win a **Grammy Award** in the Best World Music Album category for his participation in **Mickey Hart's Planet Drum**.
 
• For his immense contribution to Indian classical music, he was conferred with the **Padma Shri** in **2002** and the **Padma Bhushan** in **2014** by the Government of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhimsen Joshi**

 
 
• He was a legendary vocalist of the **Kirana Gharana** in **Hindustani classical music** and was awarded India's highest civilian honor, the **Bharat Ratna**, in **2008**.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Shivkumar Sharma**
 
 
• He was a master of the **Santoor**, a folk instrument from Jammu and Kashmir, which he modified and established as a mainstream **classical instrument**.
 
 
 
• **T. M. Krishna**
 
 
• He is a prominent **Carnatic vocalist**, author, and social activist who was awarded the **Ramon Magsaysay Award** in **2016** for using music as a tool for social reform.
